memoryText: This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Matthew 17:5 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
The Father spoke these words from a bright cloud on the mountain. Peter had just suggested building three tents, one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. The Father interrupted him.

“This is my beloved Son.” The Father identifies Jesus. He is not a prophet among prophets or a teacher among teachers. He is the Son, and the Father loves him. This is the same voice that spoke at the baptism, now speaking to the disciples directly.

“With whom I am well pleased.” The Father delights in the Son. Jesus’ obedience, his life, and his mission please the Father. And because we are in Christ, the Father’s delight in the Son reaches us.

“Listen to him.” This is the addition, and it is a command. Moses and Elijah, the law and the prophets, were great. But now the final word has come in the Son. Hebrews 1:1-2 says that God spoke in many ways long ago by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son. We are not to listen to Jesus alongside other equal voices. We are to listen to him above all.

What does it mean to listen to him? Not just to hear, but to obey. The disciples fell on their faces in fear, and Jesus came and touched them and said, “Rise, and have no fear.” The one we are told to listen to is gentle. When you read the Gospels this week, imagine the Father saying, “Listen to him.”
weekInReview: This week you moved from the quiet parables to the great confession. You heard Jesus teach that the kingdom starts small, like a mustard seed, and is worth more than all you own. You watched him feed five thousand and walk on the sea, and you saw Peter step out and sink. You read that defilement comes from the heart, that a Gentile woman showed great faith, and that Peter confessed, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” You saw Jesus begin to speak of the cross and call his followers to take up theirs. On the mountain you saw him transfigured, and heard the Father say, “Listen to him.” You then learned about humility, correction, and forgiveness. The psalms framed it: Psalm 25 asked to be taught, Psalm 2 crowned the Son, and Psalm 110 showed a king and priest at God’s right hand.
reflectionQuestions: Peter confessed that Jesus is the Christ, and almost immediately rebuked him for talking about the cross. Where are you tempted to want a Jesus without a cross?
The Father said, “Listen to him.” What does listening to Jesus look like in your daily routine?
Jesus told Peter to forgive seventy-seven times. Whom do you find hardest to forgive, and how does knowing how much you have been forgiven change that?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you listen to his beloved Son and obey.
Thank him for the glory shown and the cross carried.
